{{one source |date=May 2024}}
In algebra, an '''action of a [[monoidal category]]''' <math>(S, \otimes, e)</math> on a category <math>X</math> is a [[functor]]
:<math>\cdot: S \times X \to X</math>
such that there are natural isomorphisms <math>s \cdot (t \cdot x) \simeq (s \otimes t)\cdot x</math> and <math>e \cdot x \simeq x</math>, which satisfy the coherence conditions analogous to those in <math>S</math>.<ref>{{harvnb|Weibel|2013|loc=[http://www.math.rutgers.edu/~weibel/Kbook/Kbook.IV.pdf Ch. IV], [{{GBurl|Ja8xAAAAQBAJ|p=235}} Definition 4.7.]}}</ref> <math>S</math> is said to act on <math>X</math>. 

Any monoidal category <math>S</math> is a [[Monoid (category theory)|monoid object]] in [[Category of small categories|<math>\mathsf{Cat}</math>]] with the monoidal product being the [[Product category|category product]]. This means that <math>X</math> equipped with an <math>S</math>-action is exactly a [[nlab:module+over+a+monoid|module over a monoid]] in <math>\mathsf{Cat}</math>. 

For example, <math>S</math> acts on itself via the monoid operation <math>\otimes</math>.
